posts.name: Baskaran Nadar
posts.cooked:
While going through the recently released NPPE_1.x, I couldn’t help but notice a slightly uneasy feeling.

The questions seemed very approachable and student-friendly.

That made me wonder—are you planning a tougher surprise in the OPPE?

Just hoping this isn’t a case of a “demo vs delivery” mismatch.

Public Tests vs Private Tests

Many years ago, when John — a computer salesman from the 1970s — passed away, he arrived at the gates of St. Peter. St. Peter told him he had a choice: Heaven or Hell.

John, being a practical man, asked if he could visit both before deciding.

First he visited Heaven. There he saw elderly men sitting quietly, meditating and discussing serious philosophical ideas. It looked peaceful, but rather solemn.

Then he was taken to Hell. To his surprise, he saw lively pubs, music, dancing, laughter — people having a wonderful time.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
As pointed out, this NPPE is nothing but last term’s OPPE. There is no change in the questions. If you find this easy, you would have found last term’s OPPE easy.

I cannot comment on how you will find this term’s OPPE, since that is your personal subjective view and no one can predict that. However, the format and level will be similar. The questions can never be “same” of course, it can only be of similar level. However it has been observed that students find questions of similar level to suddenly feel harder when in the actual OPPE setting. It is more about your mentality and ability to work under pressure (OPPE is for 2 hours, not 7 days like NPPE) and when your actions have consequences (OPPE is graded, unlike NPPE).

Also, I personally do not appreciate the tone this message is set in, instead of antagonizing the course or the course team, it would be more beneficial to focus on preparation for the OPPE. Learning and being proficient in shell usage will benefit no one else other than you.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Baskaran_Nadar:

That made me wonder—are you planning a tougher surprise in the OPPE?

The course team is not here to give ‘surprises’. Plus, we have already shared enough resources, that also includes previous term papers for students to practice. As you would be moving forward to degree level, be aware that most other courses don’t even share previous term OPPE qs. Here, there are 50+ questions on VM, previous term papers, and extra questions shared by TAs.

posts.name: Baskaran Nadar
posts.cooked:
Once upon a time, Test cricket was the norm. It carried with it a certain elegance, a quiet nobility.

Played in county clubs, it was as much about the spirit of the game as it was about skill—an occasion enjoyed by people who would never quarrel over petty things.

Of course, times changed. Today, we “organize” games for many reasons, not all of them aligned with the spirit of sport.

I am reminded of what happened to those classic Test matches when I look at the current coding culture.

Fifty years ago, coding was limited to a few—but they were of a different calibre.

Now everyone is writing, and everyone is testing…
(testing what, one may wonder).
